subject: mathematics

resources.title: Calculus Volume 1
resources.notes: Functions, limits, derivatives, integration.

resources.title: Introductory Statistics
resources.notes: One-semester introductory statistics text covering descriptive statistics, probability, random variables, distributions, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing; assumes intermediate algebra.

resources.title: Single Variable Calculus
resources.notes: Independent-study calculus course with worked material and assessment.

resources.title: Multivariable Calculus
resources.notes: Vector and multivariable calculus; follows single-variable calculus.

resources.title: Calculus Open Textbook
resources.notes: Calculus text with guidance into linear algebra, differential equations, discrete mathematics, numerical methods and statistics.

resources.title: Linear Algebra
resources.notes: Independent-study matrix and vector-space curriculum with problem-solving videos, solutions and exams.

resources.title: Linear Algebra
resources.notes: Proof-oriented treatment of vector spaces, linear maps, determinants, eigenvalues, inner products and canonical forms.

resources.title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
resources.notes: Probability, Bayesian and frequentist inference, regression, simulation and statistical computing.

resources.title: Mathematics for Computer Science
resources.notes: Discrete mathematics, proofs, sets, functions, relations, modular arithmetic, graphs, counting and discrete probability. Number theory content is not mapped because number_theory is not canonical.

resources.title: Differential Equations
resources.notes: Ordinary differential equations with analytical, graphical and numerical solution methods and physical-system modeling.

resources.title: Differential Equations
resources.notes: 2024 ESG version equivalent to MIT 18.03.

resources.title: Introduction to Numerical Analysis
resources.notes: Root finding, interpolation, approximation, integration, differential equations and numerical linear algebra.

resources.title: Introduction to Numerical Methods
resources.notes: Graduate numerical methods emphasizing accuracy, efficiency, conditioning and stability; surveys nonlinear optimization.

resources.title: Real Analysis
resources.notes: Rigorous analysis and proof construction.

resources.title: Modern Algebra
resources.notes: First course in abstract algebra covering groups, quotient groups, finite abelian groups and Sylow theorems.

resources.title: Complex Variables with Applications
resources.notes: Complex analytic functions, Cauchy theory, Taylor and Laurent series and applications; multivariable calculus and differential equations prerequisites prevent downward mapping.

resources.title: Introduction to Topology
resources.notes: Topological spaces, continuity, connectedness, compactness, separation axioms and fundamental group; prior real analysis is required.

resources.title: Algebraic Topology I
resources.notes: Graduate topology covering singular homology, CW complexes, homological algebra, cohomology and Poincare duality.

resources.title: Topics in Combinatorial Optimization
resources.notes: Graduate/PhD-oriented advanced combinatorial optimization covering matchings, flows, matroids and min-max relations.

resources.title: arXiv Mathematics
resources.notes: Research/preprint layer; individual paper quality and license must be evaluated.

known_gaps: Foundation and beginner coverage remains intentionally sparse for advanced fields when an age/level-appropriate authoritative curriculum has not been verified; university courses are not mapped downward merely to increase coverage.
Geometry still needs dedicated exact-cell strengthening; specialist graduate/research coverage remains uneven across several branches.
Number theory is content within some resources but is not a canonical ATLAS Mathematics subsubject, so it is not used as a coverage mapping key.
Some matrix cells such as graduate/research arithmetic or pre-algebra are taxonomy artifacts rather than sensible curriculum targets and should not be padded with unrelated advanced resources.
Research repositories provide literature access but do not by themselves establish expert readiness without item-level review, retrieval verification, provenance and applied assessment.
